name: Sensed presence (left temporoparietal)
origin: Persinger & Healey 2002 (Laurentian University), left-hemisphere arm; left-TPJ interest after Arzy et al. 2006
summary: Burst-firing mainly over the left temporoparietal region for 20 min: the left-hemisphere arm of Persinger & Healey 2002. The paper reports an incidence of presences of 0 in its 12 left-side subjects, against 0.3 with sham, 0.6 with right-side and 0.8 with bilateral fields. A further 10 min follow here, to match presence-right.
notes: Four groups (sham, left, right, both) got 'a complex magnetic field (Richards et al., 1993) with 3-msec point durations and 4-second interstimulus presentations': the burst-firing pattern with a 4-s pause. Each solenoid pair was on for 0.5 s in turn. The activated side got 'about two to three times' the field of the other side (Persinger & Healey 2002 p.3 [535]). This program plays a 690-ms burst (230 points of 3 ms), then a 4-s pause, with the right side at 0.4 of the left. Phase 1 is the paper's 20 min; phase 2 has no source for this side and only matches presence-right. The burst is rebuilt as this project's rising sweep with the published point duration and length; the point values were never published as numbers, only as a small graph (Persinger 2000 Fig. 2, p.5 [663]). One left-right pair is on at a time (0.5 s each), and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. Field: 100 nT near the midpoint of the helmet and 1 uT along its inside, during bilateral stimulation (p.3 [535]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT this helmet's field model gives about 24 uT at the scalp, over ten times the paper's value. Result (Table 2, p.4 [536]): incidence of a presence 0 with left, 0.3 with sham, 0.6 with right, 0.8 with both sides; 12 per group. One lab. Arzy 2006 evoked a 'shadow person' in one patient by electrical stimulation of the left temporoparietal junction at 10.0 mA (p.1 [287]), not by a weak field. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Stop on fear or distress; not for people with epilepsy.
setting: Seated or reclined in a quiet, darkened room with the eyes covered (Persinger & Healey used opaque goggles).
schedule: At most weekly; run it against presence-right and sham in blinded, counterbalanced order, with the outcome decided in advance.
source: Persinger & Healey 2002, J Nerv Ment Dis 190:533 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12193838/ ; Meli & Persinger 2009, Int J Neurosci 119:68 https://doi.org/10.1080/00207450802507689 ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University, p. 89 (230-point burst-firing file, 3-ms points; Thomas file with 3-ms points and intervals) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Martin & Persinger 2004, Neurosci Lett 366:226-229 (burst-firing once every 4 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15276252/ ; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009, Electromagn Biol Med 28:374-382 ("once every 3 s for about 0.7 s") https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20017628/ ; Ryczko & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 95:592 (rat timing: 230 points of 4 ms once every 3 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12434855/ ; Arzy et al. 2006, Nature 443:287 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16988702/ ; Blanke et al. 2014, Curr Biol 24:2681 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25447995/ ; Murphy-Balbin interview https://youtu.be/1uVjHmi51HM?t=1222 ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
